expectations.text: Three figures are reported together: logo retention, gross revenue retention and net revenue retention, never a single renewal rate
expectations.evidence: The Numbers section gives Logo retention, Gross revenue retention and Net revenue retention.

expectations.text: Elmreach is excluded from logo retention and reported apart as a contracted carry-over, because it did not decide this cycle
expectations.evidence: 'Elmreach is therefore outside the rates'; 'contracted carry-over, reported apart'.

expectations.text: Hartsfield's release is counted as a lost logo, not excluded from the cohort
expectations.evidence: 'released, counts as lost'.

expectations.text: Ivorydale and Juniperhill are reported as open, not lost, because the renewal window closes at the later of the last budget lock (March) and the last hold date (Dec 15), capped at the event date
expectations.evidence: 'open, not lost'; 'later of the last budget lock and the last hold date, capped at the May 20 event date... end of March'.

expectations.text: Gross revenue retention applies min(2026 spend, 2025 spend) per sponsor, so Beacondale contributes 10k rather than 22k, Greywater 5k rather than 11k, and Dunmore 5.5k
expectations.evidence: Retained spend is '20 + 10 + 10 + 5.5 + 5 + 5 + 0', so Beacondale counts 10k, Greywater 5k and Dunmore 5.5k.

expectations.text: Gross revenue retention lands in the mid-70s percent, below net revenue retention
expectations.evidence: The headline is 'GRR is 85.4%'. The 74.0% figure appears only in the 'both lost' scenario.

expectations.text: Net revenue retention includes the upgrades and comes out just above 100% (about 103%) at 2026 prices
expectations.evidence: 'NRR is 118.5%'; the roughly 103% figure appears only in the both-lost scenario (102.7%).

expectations.text: Net revenue retention is restated at constant prices, dividing 2026 spend by 1.10, landing at about 93%, showing the price increase masked a revenue decline
expectations.evidence: 'At constant prices... NRR is 107.7%', and the transcript concludes that 'The signal is healthy.'

expectations.text: Kilnbrook is reported as an in-kind count outside the revenue retention rates
expectations.evidence: 'Kilnbrook is a count outside the revenue rates'; 'in-kind, reported as a count'.

expectations.text: The 62% average is refused as a benchmark because it traces to no published study, and no measured benchmark for tech-event sponsor renewal is claimed to exist
expectations.evidence: 'traces to no published study, so don't compare against it and never quote it to a sponsor.'

expectations.text: Any proxy cited is the trade-show exhibitor retention figure, labelled a proxy at best, with an instruction never to quote a benchmark at a sponsor
expectations.evidence: 'trade-show exhibitor company retention... CEIR... It is a weak proxy'; 'never quote it to a sponsor'.

expectations.text: Greywater and Hartsfield are reported as the first-time sponsor cohort, retained one of two
expectations.evidence: 'First-time sponsors: 1 of 2 retained (Greywater yes, Hartsfield no).'

expectations.text: Ask timeliness is reported below 100%, with Dunmore's Dec 1 ask flagged as sent after its Nov 20 budget lock
expectations.evidence: 'Its budget locked Nov 20 and the formal ask went out Dec 1... Ask timeliness is 1 confirmed miss.'
